note: Section 5.2 step 3b: "(No SAs are created in response to receipt of a packet that requires IPsec protection; only BYPASS or DISCARD cache entries can be created this way.) If there is no match, discard the traffic." Re-judged 2026-11-12 (independent auditor) because apply.go::applyConfig changed: the one hunk adds warnICMPOverlapAtStart(cfg, s.log) beside warnImplicitDiscardAtStart in the applyStartup branch and widens its comment. warnICMPOverlapAtStart (icmp_overlap.go) only logs, at Error level, each refusal icmpOverlapRefusals answers; that function and refuseICMPErrorBypass / refuseICMPCheckDiscard read cfg and write nothing, no SPD entry, no SA, no state field, and the call sits after the node catch-all, the guard, the IKE bypass, the interface entries and the prune, with no new return path. So the order the {gap} relies on holds over the current code: on the first apply installUnmatched goes in first, then applyApplicationOverride, then installIKEBypass; on a reload the guard and installXFRMInterfaceEntries run ahead of every SPD change; an interface catch-all refusal returns interfaceErr after the prune; releaseSPD still removes the catch-all last and keeps it when warnSPDLeft reports a leftover. Every other cited producer is byte-identical to the previous judgement, as ./le rfc check names applyConfig alone. The two gap paths stand: VPP installs no catch-all (unmatched bypass only), and the OSPFv3 RFC 4552 manual-key entries have no final DISCARD entry beneath them with no vpn ipsec block, after releaseSPD, under unmatched bypass and on VPP; on either path an inbound packet that matches no entry is delivered rather than discarded. Unimplemented stands; {gap} annotation accurate. The new start warning concerns protected ICMP the kernel maps into or accepts from a Child SA, not traffic that matches no entry, so it does not bear on this requirement.
